proposals.evidence: DEDR4422 gives Kannada peṟe ‘crescent moon’, Kota per ‘new moon’ and Tamil piṟai ‘crescent moon’. Betta Kurumba pəri ‘moon’ is a comparative extension to this lunar noun family; the source’s generic moon gloss is broader than the dictionary’s lunar-phase senses. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR561 gives Kannada ugur, Tulu uguru, Kodagu oy and Kurukh orᵒx finger-nail. Survey uguru/ugarɨ and glide variants are comparative regional matches, with initial v-/a- and medial-y notation preserved. Kurukh orox matches the corrected rhotic spelling; the primary explicitly rejects Grignard’s oṛᵒx, so survey retroflex-r forms are held separately. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR273 gives Kannada avva/avve/abbe mother, Kota av, Kodagu avvë and Gondi avva/avā/avval, with Tamil avvai and Telugu avva. These complete southern survey avv-/abb-/auv- responses fit that mother kinship family, retaining source vowels. The Prakrit avvā comparison and nursery-word character leave the exact transmission history open; divergent Irula agg-/aŋg- forms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
